covers: The three DMA verbs of the Sega 315-5313, started by a second control word with code bit 5 and told apart by the top bits of register 0x17, so the key is that register's value range

entries.name: 68k to VDP DMA
entries.description: Copies words from 68000 address space to VRAM, CRAM or VSRAM at once.
entries.behaviour: Runs when register 0x17 bit 7 is clear, DMA is enabled (register 0x01 bit 4) and the code is a write (1 VRAM, 3 CRAM, 5 VSRAM); otherwise nothing happens. It moves the length registers' words from the source registers to the control address, adding register 0x0F per word. A VSRAM transfer stops at address 0x80.

entries.name: VRAM fill
entries.description: Arms a fill that the next data port write performs.
entries.behaviour: Armed when register 0x17 bits 7 and 6 are 10, DMA is enabled (register 0x01 bit 4) and the code is 1, 3 or 5. The next data port write stores its low byte, then its high byte length plus 1 times, stepping by register 0x0F, always in VRAM. A control write cancels it; otherwise every data write fills again.

entries.name: VRAM copy
entries.description: Copies bytes inside VRAM at once.
entries.behaviour: Runs when register 0x17 bits 7 and 6 are set, DMA is enabled (register 0x01 bit 4), and code bit 4 is set or the code is 1. It copies the length registers' bytes from the VRAM byte address in registers 0x15 and 0x16 to the control address, stepping by register 0x0F; no register is updated afterwards.
